answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond before it may trade or vote. A vertex in the trust graph gains influence only after counterparties complete transactions and leave a signal backed by their own bonds; copied accounts cannot instantly inherit that history. If a sybil cluster is exposed, linked bonds are slashed, so an attacker must lock up capital for many identities and risks losing it. Even a jade-colored profile earns no trust without costly, verified participation.
